workout.warmup: None needed - the walk is the session. Start easy.
workout.coach_note: You caught a real error and you were right to. I built you a full lower day 48 hours after Sunday's lower session, which is too soon, and it would have been your fourth session in five days - Friday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday - which trips your own 4-in-5 rule. My first instinct to make today easy was correct, I just had the wrong reason for it. It is not your back that needs the day, it is your legs: your hamstrings were down to 7 reps by the last set on Sunday and you have trained four of the last six days while traveling and under-slept. So today is short and genuinely easy. The one thing that IS worth doing is the scapular work, because that tissue has now failed twice in ten weeks and gentle blood flow on day four helps a strain rather than hurting it. Thirty minutes, nothing heavy, no legs. Your full lower session is built and waiting for tomorrow - squats at 185 for 4x8, and the 80 lb leg curl you earned. Wednesday puts you 72 hours off Sunday, which is what that session deserves.
workout.finisher: None. Do not add anything to this.

exercises.name: Walk - Easy
exercises.detail: 20-25 min. Incline treadmill at 3.0-3.3 mph / 4-6%, or just walk outside.
exercises.note: Conversational pace the whole way. If you would rather get it outdoors than on a treadmill, do that - you mentioned wanting to put up 8-10k steps on travel days and this counts. The point is circulation and moving your thoracic spine, not a training effect.

exercises.name: Scapular Rehab Block - PAIN-FREE ONLY
exercises.detail: 3 rounds: Band Pull-Apart x 20 (light), Prone Y-Raise bodyweight x 12, Wall Slide x 10
exercises.note: This is the actual purpose of today. Day 4 on a muscle strain is where gentle, loaded-but-light movement starts speeding recovery instead of interfering with it. LIGHT band - lighter than you think, you should be able to do 20 without strain. Y-raise face down with no weight at all, thumbs up, lift from the lower trap rather than shrugging. Wall slides with your back flat and forearms tracking the wall. The rule is absolute: pain-free or you stop. Dull working sensation is fine, sharp is not.

exercises.name: Thoracic Mobility
exercises.detail: Foam roll upper back x 8 slow passes, then Open Book rotation x 8/side
exercises.note: Roll the mid-back only, above the ribs and below the neck - do NOT roll your lower back. Open books: lie on your side, knees stacked and bent, arms straight out in front, open the top arm across your body and follow it with your eyes, breathe out at the end range. A stiff thoracic spine forces the scapular stabilizers to work harder to get range they should be getting from the joint, which is plausibly part of why that tissue keeps failing.

exercises.name: Light Core
exercises.detail: 2 rounds: Dead Bugs x 12/side, Bird Dog x 10/side
exercises.note: Optional, and only if you feel like it. No side planks - propping on the elbow loads the shoulder girdle on the bad side. Low back stays pressed flat on the dead bugs, reach long rather than high on the bird dogs.
